# Proposal 4 · §17–20 EPUB → MVP

DESIGN PROPOSAL · PART 4 OF 5 · §17–20

## 17 EPUB-specific considerations

| Content | Handling |
|---|---|
| EPUB 2 vs 3 | Both. The navigation document first, NCX as fallback. EPUB 3 landmarks, page-list and noteref semantics are used when present; media overlays are ignored in MVP. |
| Reflowable | The core path: each spine item laid out in CSS columns. |
| Fixed layout | Pages scaled to fit, spreads per rendition:spread, zoom by pinch and ⌘+. Typography controls are disabled, with one line of explanation in Aa. |
| Images | Fit within the column and page height, never split across pages. Click or double-tap opens a zoomable view. |
| Tables and code | May exceed the column: they scroll horizontally inside a container with a fade at the edge. Tables break between rows across pages; code keeps its whitespace and is never hyphenated or justified. |
| Footnotes | Noterefs open a peek. Referenced epub:type="footnote" asides are taken out of the flow. |
| Links | Internal: jump, push history, show the Back chip. External: system browser. Scripts in books are disabled in MVP. |
| Embedded fonts | Used by default; obfuscated fonts are decoded; failures fall back to Literata silently. |
| RTL | Page progression honoured; the UI stays in the app’s language; bidi text follows the book’s dir attributes. |
| Vertical writing | vertical-rl supported, paginated by default, ruby preserved. |
| Long chapters | Paginate around the visible region first and the rest when idle; locations are marked “≈” until done; chapters over ~1 MB are split into virtual sections at element boundaries. |
| Large books | Read from the zip on demand, never fully unpacked in memory; only the current spine item and its neighbours are loaded; the search index is persisted. |

**Publisher styles versus reader preferences.** The rule is the publisher decides structure; the reader decides comfort. Structure is respected: heading hierarchy, emphasis, small caps, drop caps, poetry indentation, alignment of special blocks, images and tables. Comfort belongs to the reader: font size (absolute sizes are converted to relative units), body line height, text and background colours, page margins and measure. Book CSS is sanitised — no scripts, no network requests, no fixed positioning. Version 1.1 adds a three-way Publisher styles setting for books that still misbehave.

## 18 Plugin architecture

**Goal:** a small, stable core, with new capabilities added through declared slots. Extensions never reach into the page or the chrome S5.

**Structure.** The trusted core (reading engine, library, annotation store, search index, UI shell) exposes a versioned, asynchronous Host API. Each extension runs in its own sandboxed worker with no DOM access. Any UI it contributes renders in a sandboxed frame styled by Linen’s style kit, so extension panels look native without touching native UI. As in code editors, extensions activate lazily on declared events.

```
{ "id": "org.example.dictionary", "version": "1.2.0",
  "engines": { "linen": "^1.0" },
  "activation": ["onCommand:define"],
  "contributes": {
    "commands":         [{ "id": "define", "title": "Define" }],
    "selectionActions": [{ "command": "define", "when": "selection.words <= 3" }],
    "navigatorTabs":    [{ "id": "definitions", "title": "Definitions" }] },
  "permissions": ["book.selection", "network:api.dictionaryapi.dev"] }
```

| Capability | Where it appears | Release |
|---|---|---|
| Commands | Command palette; user-assigned shortcuts | **MVP** |
| Selection actions | “⋯” in the selection bar and the context menu | **MVP** |
| Custom panel | One Navigator tab per extension | **MVP** |
| Themes | Declarative token packs, listed with the built-in themes | **MVP** |
| Annotation export and events | Export menu in Notes; read-only created / changed / deleted events | **MVP** (Markdown built in) |
| Dictionary, translation | A lookup provider that renders into a peek | 1.1 |
| Metadata providers | Book info in the library | 1.1 |
| Reading statistics | Read-only session events → a Navigator tab | 1.1 |
| Text-to-speech | Speech provider with sentence sync and a playback bar | 1.2 |
| Sync providers | Storage adapter for progress and annotations | 1.2 |
| Import | Other formats converted to EPUB before opening | Later |
| Book processing | Transforms on chapter HTML before render; output re-sanitised | Later, high trust |
| AI assistant | No special slot: a Navigator tab + selection actions + the book.text permission | Once the API is stable |

**What extensions cannot do:** inject DOM or CSS into the page or chrome, draw over text, add toolbar buttons, bind core shortcuts, show notifications while you read, or modify other extensions. The top bar has no extension slot; an extension that needs one-click access can be pinned in the ⋯ menu.

## 19 Plugin security and isolation

The model follows browser and editor extensions: deny by default, declare everything in the manifest, explain it in plain language at install, and ask again when an update wants more.

| Permission | Grants | Consent |
|---|---|---|
| (none) | Commands, themes, UI slots, 10 MB private storage | None |
| book.metadata | Title, author and identifiers of the open book | At install |
| book.selection | Selected text and its location — only when the user invokes the extension | At install |
| book.text | Full text of the open book | At install, highlighted |
| annotations.read / .write | The user’s highlights and notes | At install; write highlighted |
| library.read | Metadata of every book | At install |
| network:<host> | Requests to the listed hosts only | At install; wildcards strongly warned |
| files.import / .export | Only files the user picks in an OS dialog | Each use, through the dialog |
| background | Running without being invoked | At install, strongly warned |

**Isolation.** No raw file system, shell or native modules in MVP. Extensions cannot read each other’s storage. Frames have no same-origin access and a locked content security policy; all traffic to the core is structured messages checked against granted permissions.

**Lifecycle and versioning.** Install from file → review permissions → enabled → activated on demand → unloaded when idle → updated (new permissions ask again) → disabled or removed (removal asks before deleting the extension’s data). The Host API follows semver; the core supports the current and previous major version, and incompatible extensions are disabled at load with a reason. A signed registry comes after MVP.

**Failure isolation.** The reader never waits for an extension. Host calls time out (2 s for UI contributions, 10 s for work), CPU and memory budgets are enforced, and three crashes in ten minutes suspend the extension. Its slots show one quiet line — “Dictionary stopped responding · Restart” — and reading carries on Screen 12. Safe mode (hold ⇧ at launch) starts with every extension off.

## 20 MVP definition

| In the MVP | Scope |
|---|---|
| Opening and import | OS open, drag and drop, ⌘O; copied into the library; EPUB 2 and 3 reflowable; basic fixed layout |
| Library | Continue reading, cover grid, search, sort, remove |
| Reading | Pages and Scroll; Paper, Sepia, Night, Auto |
| Chapter navigation | Contents tab, [ ], scrubber, Back history, footnote peeks |
| Search | Incremental full-text search, grouped results, marks in the text, next / previous |
| Selection, highlights, notes | Four colours, margin notes, edit, delete with Undo, Notes tab |
| Font size and spacing | Aa popover and shortcuts |
| Progress persistence | CFI saved on every page turn (debounced 1 s), on blur and on quit |
| Plugin infrastructure | Manifest, sandbox, permissions, commands, selection actions, Navigator tab, themes, Extensions page; Markdown export as the first extension |

| Not in the first release | Why |
|---|---|
| Cloud sync | Needs storage and conflict resolution for annotations. Design the sync-provider API first so sync can be an extension. |
| Account system | No value without sync; adds onboarding and privacy burden to an offline app. |
| AI assistant | Open cost and privacy questions; depends on a proven book.text permission; fits the existing slots later. |
| Text-to-speech | A mode with its own playback UI and sentence anchoring. Screen readers cover accessibility meanwhile. |
| Advanced statistics | Invites dashboards and streaks that work against calm reading. |
| More export formats | One exporter proves the pipeline; the rest are extensions. |
| Social features | The opposite of distraction-free. |
| Ebook store, DRM | Business and licensing complexity; Linen reads files you own. |
| Collections, tags, series | Search and recency are enough for MVP-size libraries. |
| Font family, justification, hyphenation | A large test matrix against publisher CSS; defaults come first. |
| Extension marketplace | Needs signing, review and hosting; install from file until then. |
